verses.translation_en: The ignorant love food that is stale, not nourishing, putrid, and corrupt; the leftovers of others, and unclean.

verses.sanskrit: अफलाकाङ्क्षिभिर्यज्ञो विधिदृष्टो य इज्यते।यष्टव्यमेवेति मनः समाधाय स सात्त्विकः॥
verses.transliteration: aphalākāṅkṣibhiryajño vidhidṛṣṭo ya ijyateyaṣṭavyameveti manaḥ samādhāya sa sāttvikaḥ
verses.translation_en: Sacrifice is pure when it is offered by one who does not covet the fruit of it, when it is done according to the commands of scripture, and with implicit faith that the sacrifice is a duty.

verses.sanskrit: अभिसंधाय तु फलं दम्भार्थमपि चैव यत्।इज्यते भरतश्रेष्ठ तं यज्ञं विद्धि राजसम्॥
verses.transliteration: abhisaṃdhāya tu phalaṃ dambhārthamapi caiva yatijyate bharataśreṣṭha taṃ yajñaṃ viddhi rājasam
verses.translation_en: Sacrifice which is performed for the sake of its results, or for self-glorification - that, O best of Aryans, is the product of passion.

verses.sanskrit: विधिहीनमसृष्टान्नं मन्त्रहीनमदक्षिणम्।श्रद्धाविरहितं यज्ञं तामसं परिचक्षते॥
verses.transliteration: vidhihīnamasṛṣṭānnaṃ mantrahīnamadakṣiṇamśraddhāvirahitaṃ yajñaṃ tāmasaṃ paricakṣate
verses.translation_en: Sacrifice that is contrary to scriptural command, that is unaccompanied by prayers or gifts of food or money, and is without faith—that is the product of ignorance.

verses.sanskrit: देवद्विजगुरुप्राज्ञपूजनं शौचमार्जवम्।ब्रह्मचर्यमहिंसा च शारीरं तप उच्यते॥
verses.transliteration: devadvijaguruprājñapūjanaṃ śaucamārjavambrahmacaryamahiṃsā ca śārīraṃ tapa ucyate
verses.translation_en: Worship of God and the Master; respect for the preacher and the philosopher; purity, rectitude, continence, and harmlessness—all of these constitute physical austerity.

verses.sanskrit: अनुद्वेगकरं वाक्यं सत्यं प्रियहितं च यत्।स्वाध्यायाभ्यसनं चैव वाङ्मयं तप उच्यते॥
verses.transliteration: anudvegakaraṃ vākyaṃ satyaṃ priyahitaṃ ca yatsvādhyāyābhyasanaṃ caiva vāṅmayaṃ tapa ucyate
verses.translation_en: Speech that hurts no one, that is true, pleasant to listen to, and beneficial, and the constant study of the scriptures—this is austerity of speech.

verses.sanskrit: मनःप्रसादः सौम्यत्वं मौनमात्मविनिग्रहः।भावसंशुद्धिरित्येतत्तपो मानसमुच्यते॥
verses.transliteration: manaḥprasādaḥ saumyatvaṃ maunamātmavinigrahaḥbhāvasaṃśuddhirityetattapo mānasamucyate
verses.translation_en: Serenity, kindness, silence, self-control, and purity—these are the austerities of the mind.

verses.sanskrit: श्रद्धया परया तप्तं तपस्तत्ित्रविधं नरैः।अफलाकाङ्क्षिभिर्युक्तैः सात्त्विकं परिचक्षते॥
verses.transliteration: śraddhayā parayā taptaṃ tapastatitravidhaṃ naraiḥaphalākāṅkṣibhiryuktaiḥ sāttvikaṃ paricakṣate
verses.translation_en: These threefold austerities, performed with faith and without thought of reward, can truly be considered pure.

verses.sanskrit: सत्कारमानपूजार्थं तपो दम्भेन चैव यत्।क्रियते तदिह प्रोक्तं राजसं चलमध्रुवम्॥
verses.transliteration: satkāramānapūjārthaṃ tapo dambhena caiva yatkriyate tadiha proktaṃ rājasaṃ calamadhruvam
verses.translation_en: Austerity coupled with hypocrisy, or performed for the sake of self-glorification, popularity, or vanity, comes from passion, and its result is always uncertain and temporary.

verses.sanskrit: मूढग्राहेणात्मनो यत्पीडया क्रियते तपः।परस्योत्सादनार्थं वा तत्तामसमुदाहृतम्॥
verses.transliteration: mūḍhagrāheṇātmano yatpīḍayā kriyate tapaḥparasyotsādanārthaṃ vā tattāmasamudāhṛtam
verses.translation_en: Austerity done under delusion, and accompanied with sorcery or the infliction of pain upon oneself or another, may be assumed to spring from ignorance.

verses.sanskrit: दातव्यमिति यद्दानं दीयतेऽनुपकारिणे।देशे काले च पात्रे च तद्दानं सात्त्विकं स्मृतम्॥
verses.transliteration: dātavyamiti yaddānaṃ dīyate'nupakāriṇedeśe kāle ca pātre ca taddānaṃ sāttvikaṃ smṛtam
verses.translation_en: The gift that is given without thought of recompense, believing it should be made, in an appropriate place, at an opportune time, and to a deserving person—such a gift is pure.

verses.sanskrit: यत्तु प्रत्युपकारार्थं फलमुद्दिश्य वा पुनः।दीयते च परिक्लिष्टं तद्दानं राजसं स्मृतम्॥
verses.transliteration: yattu pratyupakārārthaṃ phalamuddiśya vā punaḥdīyate ca parikliṣṭaṃ taddānaṃ rājasaṃ smṛtam
verses.translation_en: That which is given for the sake of the results it will produce, or with the hope of recompense, or grudgingly—that may truly be said to be the outcome of passion.

verses.sanskrit: अदेशकाले यद्दानमपात्रेभ्यश्च दीयते।असत्कृतमवज्ञातं तत्तामसमुदाहृतम्॥
verses.transliteration: adeśakāle yaddānamapātrebhyaśca dīyateasatkṛtamavajñātaṃ tattāmasamudāhṛtam
verses.translation_en: And that which is given at an inappropriate place or time or to one who is undeserving, or with disrespect or contempt - such a gift is the result of ignorance.

verses.sanskrit: तत्सदिति निर्देशो ब्रह्मणस्त्रिविधः स्मृतः।ब्राह्मणास्तेन वेदाश्च यज्ञाश्च विहिताः पुरा॥
verses.transliteration: tatsaditi nirdeśo brahmaṇastrividhaḥ smṛtaḥbrāhmaṇāstena vedāśca yajñāśca vihitāḥ purā
verses.translation_en: Om Tat Sat is the triple designation of the Eternal Spirit, by which the Vedic Scriptures, ceremonials, and sacrifices were ordained of old.

verses.sanskrit: तस्मादोमित्युदाहृत्य यज्ञदानतपःक्रियाः।प्रवर्तन्ते विधानोक्ताः सततं ब्रह्मवादिनाम्॥
verses.transliteration: tasmādomityudāhṛtya yajñadānatapaḥkriyāḥpravartante vidhānoktāḥ satataṃ brahmavādinām
verses.translation_en: Therefore, all acts of sacrifice, gifts, and austerities prescribed by the scriptures are always begun by those who understand the Spirit with the word "Om."

verses.sanskrit: तदित्यनभिसन्धाय फलं यज्ञतपःक्रियाः।दानक्रियाश्च विविधाः क्रियन्ते मोक्षकाङ्क्षि॥
verses.transliteration: tadityanabhisandhāya phalaṃ yajñatapaḥkriyāḥdānakriyāśca vividhāḥ kriyante mokṣakāṅkṣi
verses.translation_en: Those who desire deliverance begin their acts of sacrifice, austerity, or gift with the word "Tat" (meaning "That"), without thought of reward.

verses.sanskrit: सद्भावे साधुभावे च सदित्येतत्प्रयुज्यते।प्रशस्ते कर्मणि तथा सच्छब्दः पार्थ युज्यते॥
verses.transliteration: sadbhāve sādhubhāve ca sadityetatprayujyatepraśaste karmaṇi tathā sacchabdaḥ pārtha yujyate
verses.translation_en: Sat' means Reality or the highest Good, and also, O Arjuna, it is used to denote an action of exceptional merit.

verses.sanskrit: यज्ञे तपसि दाने च स्थितिः सदिति चोच्यते।कर्म चैव तदर्थीयं सदित्येवाभिधीयते॥
verses.transliteration: yajñe tapasi dāne ca sthitiḥ saditi cocyatekarma caiva tadarthīyaṃ sadityevābhidhīyate
verses.translation_en: Conviction in sacrifice, austerity, and giving is also called Sat. So too, an action done only for the Lord's sake.

verses.sanskrit: अश्रद्धया हुतं दत्तं तपस्तप्तं कृतं च यत्।असदित्युच्यते पार्थ न च तत्प्रेत्य नो इह॥
verses.transliteration: aśraddhayā hutaṃ dattaṃ tapastaptaṃ kṛtaṃ ca yatasadityucyate pārtha na ca tatpretya no iha
verses.translation_en: Whatever is done without faith, whether it be sacrifice, austerity, gift, or anything else, is called Asat (meaning "Unreal"), for it is the negation of Sat, O Arjuna! Such an act has no significance, here or hereafter.

verses.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच
संन्यासस्य महाबाहो तत्त्वमिच्छामि वेदितुम्।
त्यागस्य च हृषीकेश पृथक्केशिनिषूदन॥
verses.transliteration:
arjuna uvāca
saṃnyāsasya mahābāho tattvamicchāmi veditum
tyāgasya ca hṛṣīkeśa pṛthakkeśiniṣūdana
verses.translation_en: Arjuna asked, "O Mighty One! I desire to know how relinquishment is distinguished from renunciation.

verses.sanskrit:
श्री भगवानुवाच
काम्यानां कर्मणां न्यासं संन्यासं कवयो विदुः।
सर्वकर्मफलत्यागं प्राहुस्त्यागं विचक्षणाः॥
verses.transliteration:
śrī bhagavānuvāca
kāmyānāṃ karmaṇāṃ nyāsaṃ saṃnyāsaṃ kavayo viduḥ
sarvakarmaphalatyāgaṃ prāhustyāgaṃ vicakṣaṇāḥ
verses.translation_en: Lord Shri Krishna replied: The sages say that renunciation is forgoing an action that springs from desire, and relinquishing is the surrender of its fruit.

verses.sanskrit:
त्याज्यं दोषवदित्येके कर्म प्राहुर्मनीषिणः।
यज्ञदानतपःकर्म न त्याज्यमिति चापरे॥
verses.transliteration:
tyājyaṃ doṣavadityeke karma prāhurmanīṣiṇaḥ
yajñadānatapaḥkarma na tyājyamiti cāpare
verses.translation_en: Some philosophers say that all action is evil and should be abandoned, whereas others maintain that acts of sacrifice, benevolence, and austerity should not be given up.

verses.sanskrit: निश्चयं श्रृणु मे तत्र त्यागे भरतसत्तम।त्यागो हि पुरुषव्याघ्र त्रिविधः संप्रकीर्तितः॥
verses.transliteration: niścayaṃ śrṛṇu me tatra tyāge bharatasattamatyāgo hi puruṣavyāghra trividhaḥ saṃprakīrtitaḥ
verses.translation_en: O best of Indians! Listen to my judgment regarding this problem. It has a threefold aspect.

verses.sanskrit: यज्ञदानतपःकर्म न त्याज्यं कार्यमेव तत्।यज्ञो दानं तपश्चैव पावनानि मनीषिणाम्॥
verses.transliteration: yajñadānatapaḥkarma na tyājyaṃ kāryameva tatyajño dānaṃ tapaścaiva pāvanāni manīṣiṇām
verses.translation_en: Acts of sacrifice, benevolence, and austerity should not be given up, but should be performed, for they purify the aspiring soul.

verses.sanskrit: एतान्यपि तु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा फलानि च।कर्तव्यानीति मे पार्थ निश्िचतं मतमुत्तमम्॥
verses.transliteration: etānyapi tu karmāṇi saṅgaṃ tyaktvā phalāni cakartavyānīti me pārtha niśicataṃ matamuttamam
verses.translation_en: But they should be done with detachment and without thought of reward. This is my final judgement.

verses.sanskrit: नियतस्य तु संन्यासः कर्मणो नोपपद्यते।मोहात्तस्य परित्यागस्तामसः परिकीर्तितः॥
verses.transliteration: niyatasya tu saṃnyāsaḥ karmaṇo nopapadyatemohāttasya parityāgastāmasaḥ parikīrtitaḥ
verses.translation_en: It is not right to give up actions which are obligatory; and if they are misunderstood, it is the result of sheer ignorance.

verses.sanskrit: दुःखमित्येव यत्कर्म कायक्लेशभयात्त्यजेत्।स कृत्वा राजसं त्यागं नैव त्यागफलं लभेत्॥
verses.transliteration: duḥkhamityeva yatkarma kāyakleśabhayāttyajetsa kṛtvā rājasaṃ tyāgaṃ naiva tyāgaphalaṃ labhet
verses.translation_en: To avoid an action out of fear of physical suffering, as it is likely to be painful, is to act out of passion, and the benefit of renunciation will not be gained.

verses.sanskrit: कार्यमित्येव यत्कर्म नियतं क्रियतेऽर्जुन।सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा फलं चैव स त्यागः सात्त्विको मतः॥
verses.transliteration: kāryamityeva yatkarma niyataṃ kriyate'rjunasaṅgaṃ tyaktvā phalaṃ caiva sa tyāgaḥ sāttviko mataḥ
verses.translation_en: He who performs an obligatory action, believing it to be a duty that ought to be done, without any personal desire to do the act or to receive any return—such renunciation is pure.

verses.sanskrit: न द्वेष्ट्यकुशलं कर्म कुशले नानुषज्जते।त्यागी सत्त्वसमाविष्टो मेधावी छिन्नसंशयः॥
verses.transliteration: na dveṣṭyakuśalaṃ karma kuśale nānuṣajjatetyāgī sattvasamāviṣṭo medhāvī chinnasaṃśayaḥ
verses.translation_en: The wise man who has attained purity, whose doubts are resolved, who is filled with the spirit of self-abnegation, does not shy away from action due to its pain, nor does he crave it due to its pleasure.

verses.sanskrit: न हि देहभृता शक्यं त्यक्तुं कर्माण्यशेषतः।यस्तु कर्मफलत्यागी स त्यागीत्यभिधीयते॥
verses.transliteration: na hi dehabhṛtā śakyaṃ tyaktuṃ karmāṇyaśeṣataḥyastu karmaphalatyāgī sa tyāgītyabhidhīyate
verses.translation_en: But since those still in the body cannot entirely avoid action, in their case, the abandonment of the fruit of action is considered as complete renunciation.

verses.sanskrit: अनिष्टमिष्टं मिश्रं च त्रिविधं कर्मणः फलम्।भवत्यत्यागिनां प्रेत्य न तु संन्यासिनां क्वचित्॥
verses.transliteration: aniṣṭamiṣṭaṃ miśraṃ ca trividhaṃ karmaṇaḥ phalambhavatyatyāgināṃ pretya na tu saṃnyāsināṃ kvacit
verses.translation_en: For those who cannot renounce all desires, the fruit of action hereafter is threefold—good, evil, and partly good and partly evil. But for him who has renounced, there is none.

verses.sanskrit: पञ्चैतानि महाबाहो कारणानि निबोध मे।सांख्ये कृतान्ते प्रोक्तानि सिद्धये सर्वकर्मणाम्॥
verses.transliteration: pañcaitāni mahābāho kāraṇāni nibodha mesāṃkhye kṛtānte proktāni siddhaye sarvakarmaṇām
verses.translation_en: I will now tell you, O Mighty Man, the five causes that must come together, according to the final decision of philosophy, for an action to be accomplished.

verses.sanskrit: अधिष्ठानं तथा कर्ता करणं च पृथग्विधम्।विविधाश्च पृथक्चेष्टा दैवं चैवात्र पञ्चमम्॥
verses.transliteration: adhiṣṭhānaṃ tathā kartā karaṇaṃ ca pṛthagvidhamvividhāśca pṛthakceṣṭā daivaṃ caivātra pañcamam
verses.translation_en: They have a body, a personality, physical organs, and manifold activities and destinies.

verses.sanskrit: शरीरवाङ्मनोभिर्यत्कर्म प्रारभते नरः।न्याय्यं वा विपरीतं वा पञ्चैते तस्य हेतवः॥
verses.transliteration: śarīravāṅmanobhiryatkarma prārabhate naraḥnyāyyaṃ vā viparītaṃ vā pañcaite tasya hetavaḥ
verses.translation_en: Whatever action a person performs, whether by muscular effort, speech, or thought, and whether it be right or wrong, these five are the essential causes.

verses.sanskrit: तत्रैवं सति कर्तारमात्मानं केवलं तु यः।पश्यत्यकृतबुद्धित्वान्न स पश्यति दुर्मतिः॥
verses.transliteration: tatraivaṃ sati kartāramātmānaṃ kevalaṃ tu yaḥpaśyatyakṛtabuddhitvānna sa paśyati durmatiḥ
verses.translation_en: But the fool, who, due to his immature judgment, supposes that it is his own Self alone that acts, perverts the truth and does not see rightly.

verses.sanskrit: यस्य नाहंकृतो भावो बुद्धिर्यस्य न लिप्यते।हत्वापि स इमाँल्लोकान्न हन्ति न निबध्यते॥
verses.transliteration: yasya nāhaṃkṛto bhāvo buddhiryasya na lipyatehatvāpi sa imā~llokānna hanti na nibadhyate
verses.translation_en: He who has no pride and whose intellect is unalloyed by attachment, even though he kills these people, he does not kill them, and his act does not bind him.

verses.sanskrit: ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं परिज्ञाता त्रिविधा कर्मचोदना।करणं कर्म कर्तेति त्रिविधः कर्मसंग्रहः॥
verses.transliteration: jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ parijñātā trividhā karmacodanākaraṇaṃ karma karteti trividhaḥ karmasaṃgrahaḥ
verses.translation_en: Knowledge, the knower, and the object of knowledge are the three incentives to action; and the act, the actor, and the instrument are the threefold constituents.

verses.sanskrit: ज्ञानं कर्म च कर्ता च त्रिधैव गुणभेदतः।प्रोच्यते गुणसंख्याने यथावच्छृणु तान्यपि॥
verses.transliteration: jñānaṃ karma ca kartā ca tridhaiva guṇabhedataḥprocyate guṇasaṃkhyāne yathāvacchṛṇu tānyapi
verses.translation_en: The knowledge, the action, and the doer differ according to their qualities. Listen to this as well.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वभूतेषु येनैकं भावमव्ययमीक्षते।अविभक्तं विभक्तेषु तज्ज्ञानं विद्धि सात्त्विकम्॥
verses.transliteration: sarvabhūteṣu yenaikaṃ bhāvamavyayamīkṣateavibhaktaṃ vibhakteṣu tajjñānaṃ viddhi sāttvikam
verses.translation_en: That knowledge which sees the One Indestructible in all beings, the One Indivisible in all separate lives, can be truly called Pure Knowledge.

verses.sanskrit: पृथक्त्वेन तु यज्ज्ञानं नानाभावान्पृथग्विधान्।वेत्ति सर्वेषु भूतेषु तज्ज्ञानं विद्धि राजसम्॥
verses.transliteration: pṛthaktvena tu yajjñānaṃ nānābhāvānpṛthagvidhānvetti sarveṣu bhūteṣu tajjñānaṃ viddhi rājasam
verses.translation_en: The knowledge that perceives the manifold existence in all beings as separate comes from passion.

verses.sanskrit: यत्तु कृत्स्नवदेकस्मिन्कार्ये सक्तमहैतुकम्।अतत्त्वार्थवदल्पं च तत्तामसमुदाहृतम्॥
verses.transliteration: yattu kṛtsnavadekasminkārye saktamahaitukamatattvārthavadalpaṃ ca tattāmasamudāhṛtam
verses.translation_en: But that which clings blindly to one idea as if it were all, without logic, truth, or insight, has its origin in darkness.

verses.sanskrit: नियतं सङ्गरहितमरागद्वेषतः कृतम्।अफलप्रेप्सुना कर्म यत्तत्सात्त्विकमुच्यते॥
verses.transliteration: niyataṃ saṅgarahitamarāgadveṣataḥ kṛtamaphalaprepsunā karma yattatsāttvikamucyate
verses.translation_en: An obligatory action done by one who is disinterested, who neither likes nor dislikes it, and gives no thought to the consequences that may follow, such an action is Pure.

verses.sanskrit: यत्तु कामेप्सुना कर्म साहङ्कारेण वा पुनः।क्रियते बहुलायासं तद्राजसमुदाहृतम्॥
verses.transliteration: yattu kāmepsunā karma sāhaṅkāreṇa vā punaḥkriyate bahulāyāsaṃ tadrājasamudāhṛtam
verses.translation_en: But even though an action involves the most strenuous endeavor, yet if the doer is seeking to gratify their desires and is filled with personal vanity, it may be assumed to originate in passion.

verses.sanskrit: अनुबन्धं क्षयं हिंसामनपेक्ष्य च पौरुषम्।मोहादारभ्यते कर्म यत्तत्तामसमुच्यते॥
verses.transliteration: anubandhaṃ kṣayaṃ hiṃsāmanapekṣya ca pauruṣammohādārabhyate karma yattattāmasamucyate
verses.translation_en: An action undertaken through delusion, with no regard to the spiritual implications, the capacity of the doer, or the potential harm that may follow, is assumed to be a product of ignorance.

verses.sanskrit: मुक्तसङ्गोऽनहंवादी धृत्युत्साहसमन्वितः।सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योर्निर्विकारः कर्ता सात्त्विक उच्यते॥
verses.transliteration: muktasaṅgo'nahaṃvādī dhṛtyutsāhasamanvitaḥsiddhyasiddhyornirvikāraḥ kartā sāttvika ucyate
verses.translation_en: But when a person has no sentiment or ego, when they possess courage and confidence, not caring whether they succeed or fail, then their action arises from purity.

verses.sanskrit: रागी कर्मफलप्रेप्सुर्लुब्धो हिंसात्मकोऽशुचिः।हर्षशोकान्वितः कर्ता राजसः परिकीर्तितः॥
verses.transliteration: rāgī karmaphalaprepsurlubdho hiṃsātmako'śuciḥharṣaśokānvitaḥ kartā rājasaḥ parikīrtitaḥ
verses.translation_en: In one who is impulsive, greedy, looking for reward, violent, impure, and torn between joy and sorrow, it may be assumed that Passion is predominant.

verses.sanskrit: अयुक्तः प्राकृतः स्तब्धः शठो नैष्कृतिकोऽलसः।विषादी दीर्घसूत्री च कर्ता तामस उच्यते॥
verses.transliteration: ayuktaḥ prākṛtaḥ stabdhaḥ śaṭho naiṣkṛtiko'lasaḥviṣādī dīrghasūtrī ca kartā tāmasa ucyate
verses.translation_en: While he whose purpose is weak, who is low-minded, stubborn, dishonest, malicious, lazy, despondent, and procrastinating—he may be assumed to be in darkness.

verses.sanskrit: बुद्धेर्भेदं धृतेश्चैव गुणतस्त्रिविधं श्रृणु।प्रोच्यमानमशेषेण पृथक्त्वेन धनञ्जय॥
verses.transliteration: buddherbhedaṃ dhṛteścaiva guṇatastrividhaṃ śrṛṇuprocyamānamaśeṣeṇa pṛthaktvena dhanañjaya
verses.translation_en: Reason and conviction are threefold, according to the quality that is dominant. I will explain them fully and separately, O Arjuna!

verses.sanskrit: प्रवृत्तिं च निवृत्तिं च कार्याकार्ये भयाभये।बन्धं मोक्षं च या वेत्ति बुद्धिः सा पार्थ सात्त्विकी॥
verses.transliteration: pravṛttiṃ ca nivṛttiṃ ca kāryākārye bhayābhayebandhaṃ mokṣaṃ ca yā vetti buddhiḥ sā pārtha sāttvikī
verses.translation_en: That intellect which understands the creation and dissolution of life, what actions should be done and what not, which discriminates between fear and fearlessness, bondage and deliverance, is Pure.

verses.sanskrit: यया धर्ममधर्मं च कार्यं चाकार्यमेव च।अयथावत्प्रजानाति बुद्धिः सा पार्थ राजसी॥
verses.transliteration: yayā dharmamadharmaṃ ca kāryaṃ cākāryameva caayathāvatprajānāti buddhiḥ sā pārtha rājasī
verses.translation_en: The intellect that does not understand what is right and wrong, and what should be done and not done, is under the sway of Passion.

verses.sanskrit: अधर्मं धर्ममिति या मन्यते तमसाऽऽवृता।सर्वार्थान्विपरीतांश्च बुद्धिः सा पार्थ तामसी॥
verses.transliteration: adharmaṃ dharmamiti yā manyate tamasā''vṛtāsarvārthānviparītāṃśca buddhiḥ sā pārtha tāmasī
verses.translation_en: And that which, shrouded in Ignorance, thinks wrong to be right, and sees everything perversely, O Arjuna, that intellect is ruled by Darkness.

verses.sanskrit: धृत्या यया धारयते मनःप्राणेन्द्रियक्रियाः।योगेनाव्यभिचारिण्या धृतिः सा पार्थ सात्त्विकी॥
verses.transliteration: dhṛtyā yayā dhārayate manaḥprāṇendriyakriyāḥyogenāvyabhicāriṇyā dhṛtiḥ sā pārtha sāttvikī
verses.translation_en: The conviction and steady concentration with which the mind, the energy, and the senses are controlled—O Arjuna!—are the result of purity.

verses.sanskrit: यया तु धर्मकामार्थान् धृत्या धारयतेऽर्जुन।प्रसङ्गेन फलाकाङ्क्षी धृतिः सा पार्थ राजसी॥
verses.transliteration: yayā tu dharmakāmārthān dhṛtyā dhārayate'rjunaprasaṅgena phalākāṅkṣī dhṛtiḥ sā pārtha rājasī
verses.translation_en: The conviction that always holds fast to rituals, self-interest, and wealth for the sake of what they may bring forth comes from passion.

verses.sanskrit: यया स्वप्नं भयं शोकं विषादं मदमेव च।न विमुञ्चति दुर्मेधा धृतिः सा पार्थ तामसी॥
verses.transliteration: yayā svapnaṃ bhayaṃ śokaṃ viṣādaṃ madameva cana vimuñcati durmedhā dhṛtiḥ sā pārtha tāmasī
verses.translation_en: And that which clings perversely to false idealism, fear, grief, despair, and vanity is the product of ignorance.

verses.sanskrit: सुखं त्विदानीं त्रिविधं श्रृणु मे भरतर्षभ।अभ्यासाद्रमते यत्र दुःखान्तं च निगच्छति॥
verses.transliteration: sukhaṃ tvidānīṃ trividhaṃ śrṛṇu me bharatarṣabhaabhyāsādramate yatra duḥkhāntaṃ ca nigacchati
verses.translation_en: Hear further the three kinds of pleasure. That which increases day by day delivers one from misery.

verses.sanskrit: यत्तदग्रे विषमिव परिणामेऽमृतोपमम्।तत्सुखं सात्त्विकं प्रोक्तमात्मबुद्धिप्रसादजम्॥
verses.transliteration: yattadagre viṣamiva pariṇāme'mṛtopamamtatsukhaṃ sāttvikaṃ proktamātmabuddhiprasādajam
verses.translation_en: Which at first seems like poison but afterwards acts like nectar—that pleasure is pure, for it is born of wisdom.

verses.sanskrit: विषयेन्द्रियसंयोगाद्यत्तदग्रेऽमृतोपमम्।परिणामे विषमिव तत्सुखं राजसं स्मृतम्॥
verses.transliteration: viṣayendriyasaṃyogādyattadagre'mṛtopamampariṇāme viṣamiva tatsukhaṃ rājasaṃ smṛtam
verses.translation_en: That which, at first, is like nectar, as the senses revel in their objects, but in the end acts like poison—that pleasure arises from Passion.

verses.sanskrit: यदग्रे चानुबन्धे च सुखं मोहनमात्मनः।निद्रालस्यप्रमादोत्थं तत्तामसमुदाहृतम्॥
verses.transliteration: yadagre cānubandhe ca sukhaṃ mohanamātmanaḥnidrālasyapramādotthaṃ tattāmasamudāhṛtam
verses.translation_en: While the pleasure that drugs the senses from start to finish, which springs from indolence, lethargy, and folly—that pleasure flows from Ignorance.

verses.sanskrit: न तदस्ति पृथिव्यां वा दिवि देवेषु वा पुनः।सत्त्वं प्रकृतिजैर्मुक्तं यदेभिः स्यात्ित्रभिर्गुणैः॥
verses.transliteration: na tadasti pṛthivyāṃ vā divi deveṣu vā punaḥsattvaṃ prakṛtijairmuktaṃ yadebhiḥ syātitrabhirguṇaiḥ
verses.translation_en: There is nothing anywhere on earth or in the higher worlds that is free from the three Qualities, for they are born of Nature.

verses.sanskrit: ब्राह्मणक्षत्रियविशां शूद्राणां च परंतप।कर्माणि प्रविभक्तानि स्वभावप्रभवैर्गुणैः॥
verses.transliteration: brāhmaṇakṣatriyaviśāṃ śūdrāṇāṃ ca paraṃtapakarmāṇi pravibhaktāni svabhāvaprabhavairguṇaiḥ
verses.translation_en: O Arjuna! The duties of spiritual teachers, the soldiers, the traders, and the servants have all been fixed according to the dominant quality in their nature.

verses.sanskrit: शमो दमस्तपः शौचं क्षान्तिरार्जवमेव च।ज्ञानं विज्ञानमास्तिक्यं ब्रह्मकर्म स्वभावजम्॥
verses.transliteration: śamo damastapaḥ śaucaṃ kṣāntirārjavameva cajñānaṃ vijñānamāstikyaṃ brahmakarma svabhāvajam
verses.translation_en: Serenity, self-restraint, austerity, purity, forgiveness, uprightness, knowledge, wisdom, and faith in God—these constitute the duty of a spiritual teacher.

verses.sanskrit: शौर्यं तेजो धृतिर्दाक्ष्यं युद्धे चाप्यपलायनम्।दानमीश्वरभावश्च क्षात्रं कर्म स्वभावजम्॥
verses.transliteration: śauryaṃ tejo dhṛtirdākṣyaṃ yuddhe cāpyapalāyanamdānamīśvarabhāvaśca kṣātraṃ karma svabhāvajam
verses.translation_en: Valor, glory, firmness, skill, generosity, steadiness in battle, and the ability to rule—these constitute the duty of a soldier. They flow from his own nature.

verses.sanskrit: कृषिगौरक्ष्यवाणिज्यं वैश्यकर्म स्वभावजम्।परिचर्यात्मकं कर्म शूद्रस्यापि स्वभावजम्॥
verses.transliteration: kṛṣigaurakṣyavāṇijyaṃ vaiśyakarma svabhāvajamparicaryātmakaṃ karma śūdrasyāpi svabhāvajam
verses.translation_en: Agriculture, the protection of cows, and trade are the duties of a trader, in accordance with his nature. The duty of a servant is to serve, which also agrees with his nature.

verses.sanskrit: स्वे स्वे कर्मण्यभिरतः संसिद्धिं लभते नरः।स्वकर्मनिरतः सिद्धिं यथा विन्दति तच्छृणु॥
verses.transliteration: sve sve karmaṇyabhirataḥ saṃsiddhiṃ labhate naraḥsvakarmanirataḥ siddhiṃ yathā vindati tacchṛṇu
verses.translation_en: Perfection is attained when one diligently attends to their duty. Listen, and I will tell you how it is attained by one who always minds their own duty.

verses.sanskrit: यतः प्रवृत्तिर्भूतानां येन सर्वमिदं ततम्।स्वकर्मणा तमभ्यर्च्य सिद्धिं विन्दति मानवः॥
verses.transliteration: yataḥ pravṛttirbhūtānāṃ yena sarvamidaṃ tatamsvakarmaṇā tamabhyarcya siddhiṃ vindati mānavaḥ
verses.translation_en: One reaches perfection by dedicating their actions to God, Who is the source of all being and fills everything.

verses.sanskrit: श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात्।स्वभावनियतं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम्॥
verses.transliteration: śreyānsvadharmo viguṇaḥ paradharmātsvanuṣṭhitātsvabhāvaniyataṃ karma kurvannāpnoti kilbiṣam
verses.translation_en: It is better to do one's own duty, however defective it may be, than to follow the duty of another, however well one may perform it. He who does his duty as his own nature reveals it, never commits a sin.

verses.sanskrit: सहजं कर्म कौन्तेय सदोषमपि न त्यजेत्।सर्वारम्भा हि दोषेण धूमेनाग्निरिवावृताः॥
verses.transliteration: sahajaṃ karma kaunteya sadoṣamapi na tyajetsarvārambhā hi doṣeṇa dhūmenāgnirivāvṛtāḥ
verses.translation_en: The duty that falls to one's lot of its own accord should not be abandoned, though it may have its defects. All acts are marred by defects, just as fire is obscured by smoke.

verses.sanskrit: असक्तबुद्धिः सर्वत्र जितात्मा विगतस्पृहः।नैष्कर्म्यसिद्धिं परमां संन्यासेनाधिगच्छति॥
verses.transliteration: asaktabuddhiḥ sarvatra jitātmā vigataspṛhaḥnaiṣkarmyasiddhiṃ paramāṃ saṃnyāsenādhigacchati
verses.translation_en: He whose mind is entirely detached, who has conquered himself, and whose desires have vanished, reaches that stage of perfect freedom through his renunciation, where action completes itself and leaves no seed.

verses.sanskrit: सिद्धिं प्राप्तो यथा ब्रह्म तथाप्नोति निबोध मे।समासेनैव कौन्तेय निष्ठा ज्ञानस्य या परा॥
verses.transliteration: siddhiṃ prāpto yathā brahma tathāpnoti nibodha mesamāsenaiva kaunteya niṣṭhā jñānasya yā parā
verses.translation_en: I will now state briefly how one who has reached perfection finds the Eternal Spirit, the state of Supreme Wisdom.

verses.sanskrit: बुद्ध्या विशुद्धया युक्तो धृत्याऽऽत्मानं नियम्य च।शब्दादीन् विषयांस्त्यक्त्वा रागद्वेषौ व्युदस्य च॥
verses.transliteration: buddhyā viśuddhayā yukto dhṛtyā''tmānaṃ niyamya caśabdādīn viṣayāṃstyaktvā rāgadveṣau vyudasya ca
verses.translation_en: Guided always by pure reason, bravely restraining himself, renouncing the objects of sense and giving up attachment and hatred; he attains peace.

verses.sanskrit: विविक्तसेवी लघ्वाशी यतवाक्कायमानसः।ध्यानयोगपरो नित्यं वैराग्यं समुपाश्रितः॥
verses.transliteration: viviktasevī laghvāśī yatavākkāyamānasaḥdhyānayogaparo nityaṃ vairāgyaṃ samupāśritaḥ
verses.translation_en: Enjoying solitude, being abstemious, having his body, mind, and speech under perfect control, and being absorbed in meditation, he becomes free—always filled with the spirit of renunciation.

verses.sanskrit: अहङ्कारं बलं दर्पं कामं क्रोधं परिग्रहम्।विमुच्य निर्ममः शान्तो ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पते॥
verses.transliteration: ahaṅkāraṃ balaṃ darpaṃ kāmaṃ krodhaṃ parigrahamvimucya nirmamaḥ śānto brahmabhūyāya kalpate
verses.translation_en: Having abandoned selfishness, power, arrogance, anger, and desire, possessing nothing of his own, and having attained peace, he is fit to join the Eternal Spirit.

verses.sanskrit: ब्रह्मभूतः प्रसन्नात्मा न शोचति न काङ्क्षति।समः सर्वेषु भूतेषु मद्भक्तिं लभते पराम्॥
verses.transliteration: brahmabhūtaḥ prasannātmā na śocati na kāṅkṣatisamaḥ sarveṣu bhūteṣu madbhaktiṃ labhate parām
verses.translation_en: When he unites with the Eternal and his soul knows the bliss of the Self, he feels no desire or regret, he regards all beings equally, and enjoys the blessing of supreme devotion to Me.

verses.sanskrit: भक्त्या मामभिजानाति यावान्यश्चास्मि तत्त्वतः।ततो मां तत्त्वतो ज्ञात्वा विशते तदनन्तरम्॥
verses.transliteration: bhaktyā māmabhijānāti yāvānyaścāsmi tattvataḥtato māṃ tattvato jñātvā viśate tadanantaram
verses.translation_en: By such devotion, he sees Me, who I am and what I am; and thus realizing the truth, he enters into My kingdom.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वकर्माण्यपि सदा कुर्वाणो मद्व्यपाश्रयः।मत्प्रसादादवाप्नोति शाश्वतं पदमव्ययम्॥
verses.transliteration: sarvakarmāṇyapi sadā kurvāṇo madvyapāśrayaḥmatprasādādavāpnoti śāśvataṃ padamavyayam
verses.translation_en: Relying on Me in all his actions and doing them for My sake, he attains, by My grace, eternal and unchangeable life.

verses.sanskrit: चेतसा सर्वकर्माणि मयि संन्यस्य मत्परः।बुद्धियोगमुपाश्रित्य मच्चित्तः सततं भव॥
verses.transliteration: cetasā sarvakarmāṇi mayi saṃnyasya matparaḥbuddhiyogamupāśritya maccittaḥ satataṃ bhava
verses.translation_en: Surrender your actions to Me, live in Me, focus your intellect on Me, and always think of Me.

verses.sanskrit: मच्चित्तः सर्वदुर्गाणि मत्प्रसादात्तरिष्यसि।अथ चेत्त्वमहङ्कारान्न श्रोष्यसि विनङ्क्ष्यसि॥
verses.transliteration: maccittaḥ sarvadurgāṇi matprasādāttariṣyasiatha cettvamahaṅkārānna śroṣyasi vinaṅkṣyasi
verses.translation_en: Fix your mind on Me, and by My grace you will overcome the obstacles in your path. But if, misled by pride, you do not listen, then you will indeed be lost.

verses.sanskrit: यदहङ्कारमाश्रित्य न योत्स्य इति मन्यसे।मिथ्यैष व्यवसायस्ते प्रकृतिस्त्वां नियोक्ष्यति॥
verses.transliteration: yadahaṅkāramāśritya na yotsya iti manyasemithyaiṣa vyavasāyaste prakṛtistvāṃ niyokṣyati
verses.translation_en: If you in your vanity think of avoiding this fight, your will shall not be fulfilled, for Nature herself will compel you.

verses.sanskrit: स्वभावजेन कौन्तेय निबद्धः स्वेन कर्मणा।कर्तुं नेच्छसि यन्मोहात्करिष्यस्यवशोऽपि तत्॥
verses.transliteration: svabhāvajena kaunteya nibaddhaḥ svena karmaṇākartuṃ necchasi yanmohātkariṣyasyavaśo'pi tat
verses.translation_en: O Arjuna! Your duty binds you. It has arisen from your own nature, and that which you do not desire to do in your delusion, you will do that very thing. You are helpless.

verses.sanskrit: ईश्वरः सर्वभूतानां हृद्देशेऽर्जुन तिष्ठति।भ्रामयन्सर्वभूतानि यन्त्रारूढानि मायया॥
verses.transliteration: īśvaraḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ hṛddeśe'rjuna tiṣṭhatibhrāmayansarvabhūtāni yantrārūḍhāni māyayā
verses.translation_en: God dwells in the hearts of all beings, O Arjuna! He causes them to revolve, as it were, on a wheel, by His mystic power.

verses.sanskrit: तमेव शरणं गच्छ सर्वभावेन भारत।तत्प्रसादात्परां शान्तिं स्थानं प्राप्स्यसि शाश्वतम्॥
verses.transliteration: tameva śaraṇaṃ gaccha sarvabhāvena bhāratatatprasādātparāṃ śāntiṃ sthānaṃ prāpsyasi śāśvatam
verses.translation_en: With all your strength, fly to Him and surrender yourself, and by His grace you will attain Supreme Peace and reach the Eternal Home.

verses.sanskrit: इति ते ज्ञानमाख्यातं गुह्याद्गुह्यतरं मया।विमृश्यैतदशेषेण यथेच्छसि तथा कुरु॥
verses.transliteration: iti te jñānamākhyātaṃ guhyādguhyataraṃ mayāvimṛśyaitadaśeṣeṇa yathecchasi tathā kuru
verses.translation_en: Thus, I have revealed to you the truth, the mystery of mysteries. Having thought it over, you are free to act as you wish.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वगुह्यतमं भूयः श्रृणु मे परमं वचः।इष्टोऽसि मे दृढमिति ततो वक्ष्यामि ते हितम्॥
verses.transliteration: sarvaguhyatamaṃ bhūyaḥ śrṛṇu me paramaṃ vacaḥiṣṭo'si me dṛḍhamiti tato vakṣyāmi te hitam
verses.translation_en: Listen to My last word once more, the deepest secret of all; you are My beloved, you are My friend, and I speak for your welfare.

verses.sanskrit: मन्मना भव मद्भक्तो मद्याजी मां नमस्कुरु।मामेवैष्यसि सत्यं ते प्रतिजाने प्रियोऽसि मे॥
verses.transliteration: manmanā bhava madbhakto madyājī māṃ namaskurumāmevaiṣyasi satyaṃ te pratijāne priyo'si me
verses.translation_en: Dedicate yourself to Me, worship Me, sacrifice all for Me, prostrate yourself before Me, and you will surely come to Me. I truly pledge to you; you are My beloved.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वधर्मान्परित्यज्य मामेकं शरणं व्रज।अहं त्वा सर्वपापेभ्यो मोक्षयिष्यामि मा शुचः॥
verses.transliteration: sarvadharmānparityajya māmekaṃ śaraṇaṃ vrajaahaṃ tvā sarvapāpebhyo mokṣayiṣyāmi mā śucaḥ
verses.translation_en: Give up your earthly duties, surrender yourself to Me alone. Do not be anxious; I will absolve you from all your sins.

verses.sanskrit: इदं ते नातपस्काय नाभक्ताय कदाचन।न चाशुश्रूषवे वाच्यं न च मां योऽभ्यसूयति॥
verses.transliteration: idaṃ te nātapaskāya nābhaktāya kadācanana cāśuśrūṣave vācyaṃ na ca māṃ yo'bhyasūyati
verses.translation_en: Do not speak this to one who has not practiced austerities, or to one who does not love, or who will not listen, or who mocks.

verses.sanskrit: य इमं परमं गुह्यं मद्भक्तेष्वभिधास्यति।भक्ितं मयि परां कृत्वा मामेवैष्यत्यसंशयः॥
verses.transliteration: ya imaṃ paramaṃ guhyaṃ madbhakteṣvabhidhāsyatibhakitaṃ mayi parāṃ kṛtvā māmevaiṣyatyasaṃśayaḥ
verses.translation_en: But he who teaches this great secret to My devotees, his is the highest devotion, and he shall surely come to Me.

verses.sanskrit: न च तस्मान्मनुष्येषु कश्िचन्मे प्रियकृत्तमः।भविता न च मे तस्मादन्यः प्रियतरो भुवि॥
verses.transliteration: na ca tasmānmanuṣyeṣu kaśicanme priyakṛttamaḥbhavitā na ca me tasmādanyaḥ priyataro bhuvi
verses.translation_en: There is no one among men who can perform a service dearer to Me than this, nor is there any man on earth more beloved by Me than him.

verses.sanskrit: अध्येष्यते च य इमं धर्म्यं संवादमावयोः।ज्ञानयज्ञेन तेनाहमिष्टः स्यामिति मे मतिः॥
verses.transliteration: adhyeṣyate ca ya imaṃ dharmyaṃ saṃvādamāvayoḥjñānayajñena tenāhamiṣṭaḥ syāmiti me matiḥ
verses.translation_en: He who will study this spiritual discourse of ours, I assure you, they shall thereby worship Me at the altar of Wisdom.

verses.sanskrit: श्रद्धावाननसूयश्च श्रृणुयादपि यो नरः।सोऽपि मुक्तः शुभाँल्लोकान्प्राप्नुयात्पुण्यकर्मणाम्॥
verses.transliteration: śraddhāvānanasūyaśca śrṛṇuyādapi yo naraḥso'pi muktaḥ śubhā~llokānprāpnuyātpuṇyakarmaṇām
verses.translation_en: Yes, he who listens to it with faith and without doubt, even he, freed from evil, will rise to the worlds which the virtuous attain through righteous deeds.

verses.sanskrit: कच्चिदेतच्छ्रुतं पार्थ त्वयैकाग्रेण चेतसा।कच्चिदज्ञानसंमोहः प्रनष्टस्ते धनञ्जय॥
verses.transliteration: kaccidetacchrutaṃ pārtha tvayaikāgreṇa cetasākaccidajñānasaṃmohaḥ pranaṣṭaste dhanañjaya
verses.translation_en: O Arjuna, have you listened attentively to My words? Has your ignorance and delusion gone?

verses.sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाचनष्टो मोहः स्मृतिर्लब्धा त्वत्प्रसादान्मयाच्युत।स्थितोऽस्मि गतसन्देहः करिष्ये वचनं तव॥
verses.transliteration: arjuna uvācanaṣṭo mohaḥ smṛtirlabdhā tvatprasādānmayācyutasthito'smi gatasandehaḥ kariṣye vacanaṃ tava
verses.translation_en: Arjuna replied: "My Lord! O Immutable One! My delusion has fled. By Your Grace, O Changeless One, the light has dawned. My doubts have been dispelled, and I stand before You ready to do Your will."

verses.sanskrit: सञ्जय उवाचइत्यहं वासुदेवस्य पार्थस्य च महात्मनः।संवादमिममश्रौषमद्भुतं रोमहर्षणम्॥
verses.transliteration: sañjaya uvācaityahaṃ vāsudevasya pārthasya ca mahātmanaḥsaṃvādamimamaśrauṣamadbhutaṃ romaharṣaṇam
verses.translation_en: Sanjaya said: "I heard this rare, wonderful, and soul-stirring discourse between Lord Shri Krishna and the great-souled Arjuna.

verses.sanskrit: व्यासप्रसादाच्छ्रुतवानेतद्गुह्यमहं परम्।योगं योगेश्वरात्कृष्णात्साक्षात्कथयतः स्वयम्॥
verses.transliteration: vyāsaprasādācchrutavānetadguhyamahaṃ paramyogaṃ yogeśvarātkṛṣṇātsākṣātkathayataḥ svayam
verses.translation_en: Through the blessing of the sage Vyasa, I heard this secret and noble science from the lips of its Master, Lord Shri Krishna.

verses.sanskrit: राजन्संस्मृत्य संस्मृत्य संवादमिममद्भुतम्।केशवार्जुनयोः पुण्यं हृष्यामि च मुहुर्मुहुः॥
verses.transliteration: rājansaṃsmṛtya saṃsmṛtya saṃvādamimamadbhutamkeśavārjunayoḥ puṇyaṃ hṛṣyāmi ca muhurmuhuḥ
verses.translation_en: O King! The more I think of that marvelous and holy discourse, the more I lose myself in joy.

verses.sanskrit:
तच्च संस्मृत्य संस्मृत्य रूपमत्यद्भुतं हरेः।
विस्मयो मे महान् राजन् हृष्यामि च पुनः पुनः॥
verses.transliteration:
tacca saṃsmṛtya saṃsmṛtya rūpamatyadbhutaṃ hareḥ
vismayo me mahān rājan hṛṣyāmi ca punaḥ punaḥ
verses.translation_en: As I recall again and again the exceeding beauty of the Lord, I am filled with amazement and joy.

verses.sanskrit:
यत्र योगेश्वरः कृष्णो यत्र पार्थो धनुर्धरः।
तत्र श्रीर्विजयो भूतिर्ध्रुवा नीतिर्मतिर्मम।।18.78।
verses.transliteration:
yatra yogeśvaraḥ kṛṣṇo yatra pārtho dhanurdharaḥ
tatra śrīrvijayo bhūtirdhruvā nītirmatirmama18.78
verses.translation_en: Wherever Lord Shri Krishna, the Prince of Wisdom, and Arjuna, the Great Archer, are, I am certain that good fortune, victory, happiness, and righteousness will follow.
